analysis.title: Americas Tobacco: NielsenIQ Data thru 10/17 - Total nicotine sales declines moderated in L2wks driven by easing volume declines
key_insights: Total US nicotine retail sales fell -1.7% y/y in the 2 weeks ended 10/17, better than -2.1% for 4 weeks and -2.2% for 12 weeks. Volume fell -5.0% (vs -5.6% over 4 weeks) while pricing rose +3.6% (vs +3.8%).

Cigarette dollar sales fell -2.7% in the last 2 weeks (vs -3.2% over 4 weeks and -3.3% over 12 weeks). Volume fell -5.7% (vs -6.2% and -6.3%) and pricing rose +3.2%. MSAi data show US cigarette volume down -3.8% over the latest 4 weeks through 10/3 (vs -4.4% over 12 weeks).
Oral nicotine (including nicotine pouches) sales grew +9.2% in the last 2 weeks (vs +9.1% over 4 weeks and +6.8% over 12 weeks). Volume rose +0.4% (vs -1.4% over 4 weeks) and pricing rose +8.7%.

By company, total nicotine sales trends improved in the last 2 weeks for BAT (flat vs -0.3% over 4 weeks), IMB (-2.1% vs -2.5%), MO (-2.3% vs -2.7%) and PM (+5.0% vs +4.8%). Japan Tobacco slowed to +0.3% from +0.8%.

MO cigarette sales fell -3.0% in the last 2 weeks (vs -3.5% over 4 weeks). Volume fell -6.7% and pricing rose +3.9%. Marlboro sales fell -3.8% in total, but -7.6% excluding Marlboro Cowboy Cut, the discounted Marlboro product MO is rolling out.

Marlboro Cowboy Cut sells at a -26.3% price discount to regular Marlboro in the last 2 weeks (vs -27.4% over 4 weeks and -31.4% over 12 weeks), despite recent $0.20/pack and $0.17/pack price increases on the brand. GS says the discount tier lets Marlboro Black be priced higher over time.

Marlboro dollar share fell -51bps y/y to 42.2%, and -214bps y/y to 40.6% excluding Cowboy Cut. MO's Basic brand sales rose over +55% on heavy relative discounting and its share rose +82bps y/y to 2.1%. GS expects Basic growth to moderate through year-end on tougher comparisons.
BAT cigarette sales fell -4.2% in the last 2 weeks on volume down -8.2%. IMB cigarette sales fell -1.7% on volume down -6.6%.

ZYN total sales (including ZYN Ultra) rose +8.4% in the last 2 weeks (vs +8.1% over 4 weeks and +3.5% over 12 weeks), and +3.6% excluding ZYN Ultra. ZYN's dollar share of oral nicotine fell -19bps y/y to 27.5%.

on! total sales rose +29.3% in the last 2 weeks, and +1.0% excluding the on! PLUS rollout. on! dollar share rose +99bps y/y to 6.4%. VELO Plus dollar share rose +589bps y/y to 11.5%, while VELO sales excluding VELO Plus fell -67%.

PM has reduced ZYN promotions. Sales on promotion were 23.6% in the 4 weeks ended 10/17 (vs 51.0% a year earlier), up from 19.4% in the 4 weeks ended 9/5. GS thinks a stepped-up promotional stance for ZYN makes sense and expects PM to keep narrowing ZYN's price gap to key competitors.

ZYN's price gap to the nicotine pouch category is +6.2% in the last 2 weeks (vs +12.0% over 52 weeks). The gap to on! is -3.1% and the gap to VELO is +16.2%. ZYN volume share of the pouch category is steady at 46.9%.

ZYN Ultra, a moist pouch GS sees as marginally better than VELO Plus, is priced -3.1% below flagship ZYN with 20 pouches per can versus 15. GS believes scanner data under-captures its distribution and expects sales to ramp. In Q4 PM plans to move new flagship ZYN shipments to 20-pouch cans.

FDA granted ZYN Modified Risk Tobacco Product status, allowing certain ZYN pouches to carry reduced-risk claims versus cigarettes. GS believes this should drive adoption of ZYN and could create a halo effect for the whole nicotine pouch category. FDA guidance also says it will not prioritize enforcement against pouch and e-vapor products with PMTAs submitted.

MO's on! PLUS (FDA-approved December 2025) competes directly with VELO Plus. It sells at a -9.0% discount to flagship on! and a +2.0% premium to the pouch category. MO is promoting it to drive trial. A 12mg strength shipped in Q3 and two new flavors are due in Q4.
E-cig/vapor category sales fell -11.8% in the last 2 weeks. Volume fell -7.0% and pricing fell -5.1%. VUSE sales rose +1.3%, JUUL fell -4.2%, Geek Bar Pulse fell -40.6%, and NJOY rose +3.8%.
Cigar category sales fell -7.2% in the last 2 weeks. MO's Middleton's rose +2.0%, while Swisher (-17.1%) and Backwoods (-12.9%) declined.
risk_factors: Tough comparisons for MO's Basic brand, where sales are up over +55%, mean growth is expected to moderate through year-end.
ZYN's dollar share fell -19bps y/y and its volume is down in the 4-week and 12-week windows, while VELO Plus is gaining share with pricing about 42.5% above a year ago.
Illicit and disposable e-cig competition and continued category volume declines (-5.0% total nicotine volume) persist.
